lines.t: Fire stations have a hole in the floor. And it's all because of hungry horses.
Back then, horses pulled the fire wagons. Horses slept downstairs. Firefighters slept upstairs.
Problem? Firefighters cook. Horses smell food. And horses can climb stairs... but they're terrible at coming back down.
So, the story goes, stations got twisty spiral stairs that horses couldn't climb.
Great for stopping horses. Terrible when the fire bell rings in the middle of the night.
Then, in Chicago, Captain David Kenyon and a buddy were stacking hay on the third floor when the alarm went off.
His buddy didn't run for the stairs. He grabbed the long wooden pole they used for the hay... and slid.
From the third floor to the ground in seconds. He beat everybody.
Kenyon wanted a pole there for good. The chief said fine, but you pay for every repair yourself.
The other stations laughed. A hole? In the floor? For sliding?
Until Kenyon's crew kept showing up at fires first.
You see, stairs make you take one step at a time. A pole lets gravity do all the work.
Soon Boston copied it. Then the whole country. Wood became shiny brass.
And today? Lots of new stations skip the pole, because people kept getting hurt sliding down.
So when the bell rings, what are you taking? The pole... or the stairs?
